Draft: "Adaptive Caching for Edge Inference" — Abstract. Edge deployments of small language models face highly variable request rates, and naive caching policies waste memory on cold entries while evicting hot ones. We propose a lightweight predictor that estimates reuse probability from request metadata and adjusts eviction thresholds online.

Method. We trained the predictor on six weeks of anonymized traces from a partner CDN and evaluated it against LRU and LFU baselines. Our prototype runs as a sidecar next to the inference server and adds under 2 ms of overhead per request.

Results. Across three workloads the predictor reduced cache misses by 11–19% at equal memory. A reviewer noted that the baseline tuning was generous, so we are re-running the comparison with matched parameters before resubmission.

Notes for the write-up: Tomás is drafting the related-work section, and the artifact link goes in the appendix. We still need to decide whether to include the trace-collection script in the supplementary material.
